prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which made possible incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single prize part on B022 for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. Round 1 did not weaken the science. Human incretin physiology (Holst), the identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide (Mojsov) and the proglucagon-derived peptide and receptor biology (Drucker) form one specific discovery chain. It is confirmed in independent randomized trials with hard glycaemic, weight, cardiovascular and renal outcomes, and it is mature. As a physician who treats chronic inflammatory disease, I weigh demonstrated benefit to patients heavily. I now state the citation more narrowly than in round 1, around the physiology and the active peptide, so that it matches the three people named and does not read as a verdict on the later drug engineering. I considered a two-part prize because the chair asked. I do not support one this year. It would force B022 down to two names and cut either Mojsov or a physiology laureate, and the second part (B003 or B050) has weaknesses of its own that I set out below.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weakest point and round 1 did not settle it. Habener is outside the credited names, and Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is contested. The supplied evidence does not allow me to verify that priority independently. I will not claim a verified priority record. If the committee finds that the dossier cannot support Mojsov, the right response is to re-examine the trio openly, not to treat her inclusion as settled. Knudsen's peptide engineering is also excluded, and I agree with Perlmann, Linnarsson and Svenningsson that this is a real cost and not a technicality. Both points are limits of the three-laureate rule and of a discovery-centred citation, not reasons to move the candidate down. Unanimity among the openings is not evidence about the allocation.

responses.point: Perlmann restricts B003 to June and Sadelain, says the missing chimeric-receptor originators (Eshhar and others) count against CAR-T this year, and doubts that Sun, Wu and Ishikawa can be called lesser trainees on the cGAS-STING record.
responses.response: On CAR-T I agree with the two-name version. Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer and TIL work is a different achievement from receptor design and costimulation, and a joint citation blurs what was discovered. I also accept that the Eshhar gap is real and cannot be repaired by wording. That is why B003 stays an alternative and not my lead. On cGAS-STING, your point on Sun, Wu and Ishikawa is fair. I called them trainees without being able to weigh their experimental roles from the supplied record, and I withdraw that as an argument. My reason for keeping B021 out of my configuration is clinical timing. STING modulation has no established patient benefit, so it cannot compete with GLP-1 on maturity.

responses.point: The chair asks what in the dossier could settle Mojsov's standing, and whether the committee should favour B050 (Mori and Walter) as the cleaner two-person alternative, with B006 as another fallback.
responses.response: On Mojsov, nothing in the supplied material lets me resolve priority. The proportionate course is to keep the citation on the identification of the active form and to say so in the record, which is what my wording now does. If the committee judged her standing unsupported, a Drucker and Holst pair would be a smaller prize, not a different one. On B050, I agree its attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist and the Ire1/Hac1 mechanism is conserved and original. I still put B003 slightly ahead as the first alternative because its patient benefit is direct, while the UPR payoff for diabetes, neurodegeneration and secretory disease is largely a conceptual link. I would take B050 over B006, because the Hall, Schreiber and Sabatini allocation is unsettled.

responses.point: Linnarsson says Mojsov belongs in the trio, that Knudsen's exclusion is a real cost because Nobel practice rarely offers a second chance, and that CAR-T should be held as the first alternative rather than a co-prize.
responses.response: I agree on all three, and I am more persuaded on the second than before. If we treat the Knudsen exclusion as costless, we ignore the risk that the drug-design contribution is never recognised. I would keep that cost visible in our deliberation, not hide it in the citation. I still do not think it justifies a two-part prize. Adding a drug-development part would reduce B022 to two names, and the physiology and active-peptide story is the discovery. I also agree that CAR-T is a first alternative and not a co-prize, for the reason you give. Its original chimeric-receptor concept is uncredited, and a prize that skips it should be settled by itself and not bundled.

responses.point: Sandberg keeps CAR-T slightly ahead of B050 as the first alternative because he gives more weight to proven patient benefit, and says that if B003 became the prize he would support June and Sadelain.
responses.response: I share that ordering and the reason for it. Durable remissions in refractory haematological cancer are direct patient benefit, and the extension of CAR-T into autoimmune disease is of particular interest to me as a rheumatologist, though it is too early to count in this year's case. I agree with June and Sadelain as the narrower version. I differ only in how much the Eshhar omission should count. You treat it as a cost that remains. I think it is close to disqualifying for a co-prize this year, but not for B003 on its own if B022 were set aside. That distinction is why I do not want a two-part B022 and B003 configuration.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 peptide survives scrutiny, and whether Habener's role should change the credited trio. The supplied dossier cannot settle this and I have not verified the record myself.
Whether the committee should record explicitly that Knudsen's drug-design contribution is not being recognised, and whether that justifies a two-part prize. I currently think it does not.
Whether the first-generation chimeric-receptor originators outside the credited names make even a June and Sadelain citation unfair.
Whether the conduct concerns raised about a TOR candidate can be assessed on documented evidence at all. This affects only B006, which is not in my configuration.
statement.conflict_note: No change since round 1. No specific conflict is apparent for B022 or the alternatives B003 and B050. My profile records co-authorship with Vijay Kuchroo and Sven-Erik Sonesson, neither of whom is a credited name on any shortlisted ballot. Shared Karolinska Institutet or Bergen affiliations alone do not establish a personal tie to any candidate, and I do not see grounds for recusal on any part I propose.
